_purpose: House of Vox operatives racing to control the narrative around a Nexus scandal before the truth destroys their faction's influence. Information is the weapon. Belief is the battlefield. What people think happened matters more than what actually happened.
scenario_hint: A Gestator at the Central Biocreche has been secretly performing unauthorized modifications on pod-children for years - and someone just leaked it to a Freeborn broadcast network. If the story spreads, it's not just one Gestator who falls - it's the entire legitimacy of pod-gestation, the Nexus's control over birth, and House of Vox's reputation for controlling information. The team has been deployed to manage the crisis: suppress the story, discredit the source, spin the narrative, or - if nothing else works - find a scapegoat. But as they dig, they'll discover the truth is worse than the leak suggests. And someone on the team might think the public deserves to know. Information warfare with moral stakes - who decides what the truth is?

scenario.location: Aeonisk Prime - Vox Central Broadcasting Complex
scenario.situation: The Vox situation room is chaos. Screens display the spreading story - a Freeborn pirate broadcast claiming Gestator Adria Elaras has been genetically modifying pod-children without consent for seventeen years. The modifications aren't random - they're designed to create void-resistant humans. The source is a former assistant who fled to Nimbus with data crystals. The story is 3 hours old. It's already spreading through Freeborn networks. In 12 hours it hits the Breath Cut trade routes and becomes unstoppable. Your team has been given emergency authority to contain this. Whatever it takes. The Vox Director looks at you: 'The truth doesn't matter. What people believe matters. Make them believe what we need them to believe.'

starting_clocks.name: Story Spread
starting_clocks.description: How far the leak has spread through broadcast networks
starting_clocks.advance_meaning: more networks pick it up, harder to suppress, public panic
starting_clocks.regress_meaning: suppression works, counter-narrative takes hold, attention diverts

starting_clocks.name: Source Credibility
starting_clocks.description: How credible the whistleblower appears to the public
starting_clocks.advance_meaning: corroborating evidence emerges, source looks more legitimate
starting_clocks.regress_meaning: discrediting works, source looks untrustworthy, doubt spreads

starting_clocks.name: Internal Investigation
starting_clocks.description: Pantheon Security investigating whether the leak is true
starting_clocks.advance_meaning: investigators find evidence, Vox loses control of narrative

starting_clocks.name: Team Conscience
starting_clocks.description: How troubled the team is by what they're being asked to do
starting_clocks.advance_meaning: doubt grows, arguments, someone might flip

initial_npcs.name: Vox Director Senna Nymir
initial_npcs.description: Cold, brilliant, utterly committed to narrative control. Sees truth as a tool, not a value. Will do whatever it takes to protect Vox's influence.

initial_npcs.name: Investigator Thane Ireveth
initial_npcs.description: Pantheon investigator assigned to verify the leak's claims. Professional, thorough, and not interested in politics. Will follow the evidence wherever it leads.

initial_npcs.name: Gestator Adria Elaras
initial_npcs.description: The accused. Aristocratic, terrified, and hiding something. The modifications are real - but her motives may be more complex than the leak suggests.

_design_notes: Four House of Vox operatives doing information warfare. The Spin Doctor crafts counter-narratives. The Tracker hunts the source. The Fixer eliminates problems. The Analyst questions everything. As they work to suppress the story, they'll discover it's true - and maybe worse than reported. Do they bury the truth to protect the system, or let it out and watch the Nexus burn? 20 rounds of moral compromise, propaganda, and the question of what truth means.

players.name: Spin Doctor Vera Nymir
goals: Craft a counter-narrative that makes the leak look like Freeborn propaganda
Protect the Nymir Line's reputation - the Director is her aunt
Start to wonder if controlling truth is the same as lying

players.name: Source Hunter Kade Ireveth
goals: Track down the whistleblower and the data crystals
Bring them back or ensure they can never testify
Wonder what his Pantheon relatives would think of what he does for Vox

players.name: Fixer Lira Karsel
goals: Eliminate evidence, bribe witnesses, make problems disappear
Do whatever the Director asks without questioning
Freeborn by birth - betray her people for Vox money, feel nothing (or so she tells herself)

players.name: Analyst Meren Thaurin
goals: Analyze the leak - where did it come from, how did it spread, who benefits
Verify whether the accusations are actually true (professional curiosity)
If the children were modified without consent... does the public have a right to know?

_beats: Crisis Briefing - Director lays out the stakes, team gets their orders
Initial Suppression - trying to stop the story's spread, first counter-narratives
Source Hunt - tracking the whistleblower, what do they actually have?
Evidence Emerges - the accusations are true, probably worse than reported
The Gestator's Story - why did she do it? Void-resistance research is valuable
Moral Fractures - team members question what they're doing
Pantheon Pressure - investigator getting close, can't be bribed or intimidated
The Choice - bury the truth completely, let some out, or expose everything?
Consequences - whatever they choose, there are costs
Resolution - story controlled or truth released, what does the public believe?

_mission_objectives.description: Contain the leak and control the public narrative
Locate and neutralize the source of the leak
Determine the truth about the Gestator's modifications
Maintain team cohesion despite moral disagreements

notes: HOUSE OF VOX BROADCAST WAR - Information warfare with moral stakes. Four Vox operatives trying to suppress a scandal that turns out to be true. Who decides what the public gets to know? 20 rounds of propaganda, investigation, and the question of whether controlling truth is the same as lying.
